newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - Ringgit hits weakest level since flotation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ringgit hits weakest level since flotation.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit took a fresh beating on Friday, hitting its lowest level against the U.S. dollar since the currency was officially floated in 1973, dealers said.
Fresh speculative selling out of Singapore pushed the currency to a record low of 2.8250 to a dollar, dealers said. It had recovered to 2.8000/50 by 0635 GMT.
Dealers said the weakness in the Indonesian rupiah has spilled over to the ringgit.
The rupiah dropped to a record low of 2,890 to the dollar on Friday after the central Bank of Indonesia allowed it float the day before.
Dealers said thin market liquidity had made it easier to push the dollar/ringgit across the key psychological level of 2.8000.
"Most of the selling came out of Singapore. Volume is thin which makes it easy to move the market," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.

"For now, it is likely that some players who were already long on the dollar may want to take some profits which may see the dollar/ringgit back to 2.8000 over the short term," said another Singapore dealer.
Talk of intervention by the central Bank Negara Malaysia at around 2.7910 earlier in the day could not be confirmed.
Dealers said the worst may not be over as regional currencies remained under pressure.
"So long as the regional crisis is not over, weakness will remain," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "European players are likely to react when they enter later."
The ringgit, like the Thai baht, the Philippine peso and the rupiah, has been hit by speculative attacks over the past month. It has lost nearly 13 percent of its value.
Technically, the ringgit is seen heading for 2.8385 with support for the dollar seen at 2.7950, dealers said.
